attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, stated as his assessment of 2025.

semantics.note: A firm retrospective observation about agents in 2025. The 'despite the hype' framing is rhetorical and changes nothing material.

contract.note: The plain reading (general-purpose agents did not consistently complete realistic multistep work, while narrow configured workflows may have) is fair and ordinary. Period limited to 2025 through Dec 20.

evidence.note: Sept 2025 version of TheAgentCompany: best configuration about 30% full completion; most tasks failed. Independent, in period.
June 2025 tau2 study: moderate single-trial success, lower consistency over repeated trials, failures on multistage tasks.
METR March 2025: near-perfect on very short tasks but under 10% on long ones, and agents could not reliably do low-skill computer work. Mostly supportive, with a short-task caveat.
Amazon's own claim of 90% reliability for narrow customer-built browser workflows. A company disclosure about a narrow case the contract excludes.

reviews.rationale: Independent 2025 evaluations (e1, e2, e3) consistently show low full-task completion and poor consistency on realistic multistep work. The only counterweight is Amazon's narrow, self-reported claim (e4), which does not meet the contradiction condition. Under the fair plain reading, the observation holds.

attribution.note: Marcus's own tally of his own predictions, in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'by my count' qualifier. The substantive commitment is that 16 of the 17 high-confidence predictions proved correct.

contract.note: Requiring an independent item-by-item check is fair, since the self-count cannot prove itself. How bundled and still-open entries are scored would decide the result.

evidence.note: Marcus's original Jan 2025 list. It defines the predictions but is his own statement, not evidence of whether they came true. Labelled company_disclosure, but it is the speaker's own text.

reviews.rationale: The packet holds only the original list, which defines the items. There is no independent outcome evidence for the seventeen entries and no item-by-item tally, so the aggregate 16-of-17 count can be neither confirmed nor refuted.

attribution.note: Marcus's own retrospective statement in his own post.

semantics.note: The firm part is that no single system solved more than 4 tasks. The 'or maybe any' parenthetical is hedged and correctly left unscored.

contract.note: Scoring only the firm upper bound and requiring task-level evidence is fair. The Dec 20 cutoff is harmless: if none qualified by year-end, none did earlier.

evidence.note: The original Dec 2024 bet text defines the ten tasks and the judging panel. Definitions only.
Independent LessWrong retrospective rates the upper bound correct at year-end, which covers Dec 20. But it gives no task-level audit or primary tests, so it falls short of the support condition.

reviews.rationale: Nothing in the packet shows any system completing five tasks, and one independent retrospective (e2) agrees with the upper bound. The contract, however, requires a comprehensive task-level assessment, which the packet lacks. The evidence leans toward support but does not settle the claim.
